listNote: The official 55 trophies as PlayStation publishes them: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden until earned; no online trophies. Names, descriptions and grades follow the official PSN list [1] as mirrored by Exophase [2] and PSNProfiles [3], which agree on every entry.
auditNote: Every guide below is written for this atlas in our own words. A bracketed number after a step is the source that step rests on; the numbered source list sits in the right rail and in the Sources tab. Sources are listed per page, not per site: each numbered entry is the single page that backs the claims cited to it.
disagreementNote: SOURCES DISAGREE on meditations: the trophy guides count 18 meditations across 10 spots [5][23], while the 100% completion checklist only asks for 15 of the 18 [19][21]. Both numbers are shown wherever meditations appear; the trophy itself tracks 18. Nine disagreements in total are recorded in the disputes list, each shown both ways with our call.

disputes.topic: How many meditations does Positive Mental Attitude need?
disputes.a: 18 meditations across 10 spots — the trophy route counts all 18, meditating as both characters where a spot allows it [5][8][23].
disputes.b: 15 of the 18 — the 100% completion checklist is satisfied with 15 [19][21].
disputes.call: Our call: plan for 18. The 15 figure is the checklist's shortcut, not the trophy's target; the PSN counter for the trophy tracks 18 [30].

disputes.topic: Is the Chapter 1 balcony meditation strictly required?
disputes.a: Treat it as required: it disappears when Chapter 1 ends, so a missed window can cost the whole playthrough [5][22].
disputes.b: Still unconfirmed whether the trophy strictly needs that one meditation [5][23].
disputes.call: Our call: do it anyway and keep a chapter-start save. The cost is two minutes; the risk is a full restart [5].

disputes.topic: How many challenges does the 100% checklist want?
disputes.a: 70 of 80 challenges — the roadmap's 100% step works to a quota, not the full list [5][7].
disputes.b: 80 challenges exist in total, and the separate trophy One Last Thing only asks for 50 of them [17][3].
disputes.call: Our call: 70 for the checklist, 50 for the trophy. Three different numbers, three different jobs — do not grind all 80 for either [7].

disputes.a: 100 locations — the trophy counts each new location once, and PSN tracks 100 [3][14].
disputes.b: 200 vehicles — the 100% route separately talks about scanning 200 vehicles with the same app [23][25].
disputes.call: Our call: both numbers are real but they belong to different counters. The trophy is the 100 locations; the 200 scans belong to the checklist route [23].

disputes.topic: Card sets: complete sets or a subset?
disputes.a: 3 complete sets — the silver wants three full sets, tracked by PSN at 3 [3][9].
disputes.b: A subset of sets — the 100% checklist reportedly accepts only part of the card sets [19][21].
disputes.call: Our call: finish 3 complete sets for the trophy; if you only need the checklist, its subset is enough [20].

disputes.topic: Which trophy pops last before the platinum?
disputes.a: A Long Road (100% completion) is the final trophy for most players [5][19].
disputes.b: The platinum itself lands the moment the other 54 are all earned, whichever is last on your run [2][1].
disputes.call: Our call: both are right. Plan as if A Long Road is last, because on most routes it is [5].

disputes.topic: How long is the platinum, really?
disputes.a: ≈200 hours in a single playthrough, difficulty 4/10 [5].
disputes.b: Adding every per-trophy time estimate in this atlas gives a much bigger number, because the estimates overlap inside shared play [3].
disputes.call: Our call: trust the ≈200-hour roadmap figure. Per-trophy hours are planning units, not additive totals [5].

disputes.topic: What does Actions Speak Louder actually count?
disputes.a: 500 choices — PSN tracks a counter of 500 against this trophy [3].
disputes.b: The exact definition is still unconfirmed: no launch guide read for this atlas had verified what a counted 'choice' is [28].
disputes.call: Our call: make choices as they arise and let the counter build across a full playthrough; do not stall progress hunting them [3][28].

disputes.topic: Let's Go Bowling: a strike, a full game, or one throw?
disputes.a: Start with a complete game at the Kolt & Associates alley, with a clean follow-through motion [26][28].
disputes.b: Whether it wants a strike, a full game or a specific throw was not settled in the sources read [2][1].
disputes.call: Our call: bowl a full game first. If it does not pop, the precise trigger is still unconfirmed in launch guides [28].
